details: For finite classes, this is the metric inequality $B(\mathcal H)\ge D^+(\mathcal H)/2$.
proof: An oriented-diameter witness of size $d$ gives two concepts whose traces differ on all $d$ witness coordinates. For any Hamming-ball center, at least one of those concepts is at distance at least $d/2$ from it. Hence $B(\mathcal H)\ge \tfrac12 D^+(\mathcal H)$.
name: Hamming Radius / Oriented Diameter
